paper.title: Principles of isomer stability in small clusters

settings.name: pseudopotentials
settings.value: soft norm-conserving (Goedecker-Teter-Hutter family) with non-linear core corrections, refs 50 (GTH 1996) and 51 (Willand et al. 2013); valence electrons Na 1, Mg 2, Al 3, Si 4, Ge 4
settings.source: paper §II Methods, refs 50-51; valence counts implied by Table 1 'Number of electrons'

settings.name: xc_functional
settings.value: PBE via Libxc; LDA for all Mg clusters

settings.name: spin
settings.value: spin-polarized for odd electron counts; even electron counts assumed singlet (spin-restricted)

settings.name: electronic_temperature
settings.value: 0 for all, except 3e-3 Ha for Mg clusters with an odd number of electrons

settings.name: structure_search
settings.value: Minima Hopping at DFT level (not reproduced by this workflow)

settings.name: eigenvalue_degeneracy_threshold
settings.value: two KS eigenvalues are degenerate if they differ by less than 1e-4 Ha
settings.source: dataset notebook all_minima_data_analysis.ipynb, property documentation cell

settings.name: point_group_analysis
settings.value: pymatgen point group with tol=0.0009 (get_pymatgen_pointgroup(filename, tol=0.0009))

unknown_settings.name: grid_spacing_hgrid
unknown_settings.source: not stated in paper §II or ESI; run a convergence scan; the cubic wavelet grid can split symmetry-degenerate levels, so it also affects gm-eigenvalue-degeneracy and gm-point-group (via relaxation)

unknown_settings.name: grid_extent_rmult
unknown_settings.source: not stated; anions have weakly bound LUMOs (e.g. Al13m1 LUMO about -0.001 Ha), so the extent matters for gap and VEA

unknown_settings.name: exact_psppar_files
unknown_settings.source: refs 50-51 name the family (GTH/HGH-K with NLCC, Willand 2013), not the file version; affects every claim slightly and the absolute energy most. Record the file used and its sha256; stored KS-energy-contributions help diagnose a mismatch

unknown_settings.name: odd_electron_magnetic_moment
unknown_settings.source: paper says 'spin polarized' for odd counts but gives no moment; use the minimal moment (mpol 1) and record it as an approximation

unknown_settings.name: mg_smearing_scheme
unknown_settings.source: only the temperature (3e-3 Ha) is stated, not the smearing function

structures.details: MCP server small_cluster_isomers, tool minima_database_extract_isomer_xyz(system=<label>, rank=<0-based> | name=<stored name>). Rank 0 is the global minimum; ranks follow the stored order (energy above GM ascending). Never build names from ranks.
structures.units: per file: header token 'angstroemd0' = Angstrom, 'atomicd0' = Bohr (all Si10p1 and 240 Si20p1 files)
structures.notes: BigDFT xyz: line 1 = natoms, units, energy (Ha); line 2 = boundary ('free'); then natoms coordinate lines; then a 'forces' block that must be dropped. The structures are BigDFT-optimized minima, so single points at these geometries are the primary test.

electronic_state_rules.charge: system label = <cluster family><suffix>; suffix m1 -> charge -1 (one extra electron), none -> 0, p1/p2/p3 -> +1/+2/+3. Use minima_database_list_systems for the family/suffix split; never regex-parse labels.
electronic_state_rules.spin: electrons = sum of valence electrons - charge; odd -> spin-polarized (minimal moment, flagged approximation); even -> spin-restricted singlet. Check the count against Table 1 'Number of electrons' (e.g. Al13m1 = 40).
electronic_state_rules.smearing: none, except Mg clusters with an odd electron count: electronic temperature 3e-3 Ha
electronic_state_rules.source: dataset notebook label legend; paper §II Methods; Table 1

reference_data.details: small_cluster_isomers tools minima_database_get_isomer_properties(system, rank|name) for per-isomer values, and minima_database_export_property_table(system, keys, max_rank) for ranked tables. Units are returned in the tool's 'units' map. Table 1 of the paper gives the same GM values rounded to 2-3 decimals.

claims.statement: The global minimum of the system has the point group listed in Table 1 (e.g. Al13^-1 is Ih).
claims.computation: Relax the stored GM geometry with BigDFT (forces < 0.5 meV/Angstrom, paper settings). Determine the point group of the relaxed geometry with pymatgen PointGroupAnalyzer at tolerance 0.0009 (dataset convention). As a control, apply the same analysis to the stored geometry; it must reproduce the stored label first, otherwise mark the claim inconclusive (definition_ambiguous).

claims.statement: HOMO-LUMO gap of the global minimum (Table 1, e.g. 1.88 eV for Al13^-1).
claims.computation: Single point at the stored GM geometry with virtual orbitals enabled; gap = LUMO - HOMO in eV. Spin-restricted systems only by default; for spin-polarized systems the paper does not define which channel is used, so mark the claim inconclusive (definition_ambiguous) unless the user fixes a definition.
claims.qualitative_property: the gap stays positive, and the order of gaps across the listed systems is preserved

claims.statement: The occupied Kohn-Sham levels of the global minimum form the degeneracy pattern listed in the dataset and Table 2 (e.g. Al13^-1: [1, 3, 5, 1, 3, 3, 4]), the basis of the 'optimal matching' argument.
claims.source: §III.B optimal matching; Table 2; dataset key Eigenvalue-degeneracy
claims.computation: From the single point at the stored GM geometry: sort the occupied KS eigenvalues and group consecutive levels that differ by less than 1e-4 Ha; the ordered list of group sizes must equal the stored list exactly.

claims.statement: Energies of the lowest isomers above the global minimum, and their order.
claims.source: dataset key Fingerprint-distance-GM[0] (energy above GM, Ha); Figs 2-7, 17-18 energy axes
claims.computation: Single points at the stored geometries of ranks 0-4 (and rank 5 as a sentinel). dE_k = E_KS(rank k) - E_KS(rank 0), in eV (1 Ha = 27.211386 eV). Verdict: each dE_k within tolerance of the stored value gives reproduced; the order of ranks 0-5 is preserved but some dE_k are outside tolerance gives reproduced_trend.

claims.statement: Vertical ionization energy of the global minimum.
claims.source: §III.B.2 definition next to eqn (6); dataset key Vertical-Ionization-energy (eV)
claims.computation: VIE = E(m-1 electrons) - E(m electrons), both at the stored m-electron GM geometry (frozen). The (m-1)-electron run follows the spin rule for its own electron count.

claims.statement: Vertical electron affinity of the global minimum.
claims.source: §III.B.2 definition next to eqn (6); dataset key Vertical-Electron-Affinity (eV; stored per isomer)
claims.computation: VEA = E(m electrons) - E(m+1 electrons), both at the stored m-electron GM geometry. For anions the (m+1)-electron state may be unbound; if its SCF does not converge, mark the claim inconclusive (unconverged).

claims.statement: Chemical hardness eta = (VIE - VEA)/2 of the global minimum (Table 1, e.g. 2.52 eV for Al13^-1).
claims.source: eqn (6); Table 1 'Chemical Hardness [eV]'; dataset key Chemical-Hardness
claims.computation: eta = (VIE - VEA)/2 using the computed values of gm-vertical-ionization-energy and gm-vertical-electron-affinity (no extra runs).

claims.statement: Average bond distance of the global minimum (Table 1 'Average bond distance [Angstrom]').
claims.computation: On the BigDFT-relaxed GM geometry (Angstrom): zeta_kl from eqn (2) with the element's tau and nu (§III.A.1); average bond distance = sum_{k != l} zeta_kl d_kl / sum_{k != l} zeta_kl. This zeta-weighted pair average reproduces the stored Coordination[1] to 1e-10 Angstrom on stored geometries (checked on 8 isomers); the paper's prose suggests a per-atom average, which does NOT match the dataset.
claims.qualitative_property: metallic GMs shorter than bulk tau, covalent GMs longer (paper §III.A.1)

claims.statement: Final Kohn-Sham energy of the global minimum.
claims.computation: Total energy from the single point at the stored GM geometry. It is reported as a diagnostic because grid and pseudopotential file versions are unknown; compare the energy-contribution breakdown with KS-energy-contributions to locate differences.

excluded_claims.statement: The listed structure is the true global minimum of the potential energy surface.
excluded_claims.reason: needs a Minima Hopping search; only 'lowest among supplied structures' is testable (isomer-energy-ordering)
not defined in the paper text; which relaxed (m-1) structure was used is not stated

excluded_claims.statement: Shape factor S (eqn 3), surface/volume ratio and fingerprint distances.
excluded_claims.reason: geometric descriptors of the stored structures, not DFT results; they change only through relaxation, which gm-point-group and gm-average-bond-distance already test

excluded_claims.statement: Correlation trends in Figs 2-7 and 17-18 across whole potential energy surfaces.
excluded_claims.reason: would need thousands of single points; run isomer-energy-ordering on chosen systems instead

excluded_claims.statement: Any property of the Al12Si systems other than energies, gap, point group and degeneracy of stored data.
excluded_claims.reason: the dataset stores only 11 of 18 keys for Al12Si (no VIE/VEA/hardness), so there is no reference

known_notes: Table 1 'KS DFT degeneracies' lists the distinct degeneracy values, with starred numbers marking approximate degeneracies (Table 1 caption); Table 2 and the dataset list every occupied level in order. The two are different notations, not a discrepancy: compare against the dataset list.
The dataset notebook documents Vertical-Electron-Affinity at a cluster-level path; the value is actually stored per isomer (the MCP tools read the correct location).
Stored isomer order is by energy above GM (Fingerprint-distance-GM[0]); in 22 systems KS-Final-energy is not strictly monotonic along that order. Use energy-above-GM values as the ordering reference.
The xyz header energy can differ from KS-Final-energy by more than 1e-6 Ha (1207 minima); use KS-Final-energy as the reference.
VEA values are stored with the sign of E(m) - E(m+1) (e.g. Al13m1 GM VEA = -1.47 eV); keep that sign convention when comparing.
